# commander_enterprise_scim_push (Resource)

Use this resource to **push SCIM data** to a Keeper SCIM endpoint in a single step. You choose where the data comes from (Google Workspace, Active Directory, or a record) and whether to auto-approve teams.

## What this resource does

- When you **apply**, it runs a one-time SCIM push with your settings.
- Terraform does **not** read or delete anything on the server. It only runs the push and tracks that it happened.
- If you change **scim_id**, **source**, **record**, **auto_approve**, or **managed_company**, Terraform will run the push again with the new values.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# commander_enterprise_scim_push: one-time push of SCIM data to a Keeper SCIM endpoint.
#
# Required: scim_id, source (google | ad | record), record (record UID), auto_approve.
# Optional: managed_company (MSP only).
#
# When you apply, Terraform runs the push once. Changing any value runs the push again.
# No read or delete on the server; removing the resource only removes it from state.

resource "commander_enterprise_scim_push" "example" {
  scim_id      = "1234567890"      # ID of your SCIM configuration
  source       = "google"          # google | ad | record
  record       = "your_record_uid" # Record UID with SCIM configuration
  auto_approve = true              # true = auto-approve SCIM teams; false = require approval

  # Optional, MSP only: run in a specific managed company
  # managed_company = "Acme Corp"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `auto_approve` (Boolean) **Auto approve** SCIM teams
- `record` (String) **Record UID** with SCIM configuration
- `scim_id` (String) SCIM ID
- `source` (String) Source of SCIM data. Must be one of: `google`, `ad`, `record`.

### Optional

- `managed_company` (String) Only applies to **MSP accounts**. **Name** or **ID** of the managed company to scope this resource or data source to. Omit to use the logged-in account context.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Deterministic ID computed from scim_id, source, record, auto_approve, and managed_company.
